PENETRATING EYE INJURY 
History: 
•
Time of injury 
•
Type of incident 
•
Description of object causing injury 
•
Tetanus status 
 
Examination 
•
Visual acuity BOTH EYES 
•
Eye movement 
•
Pupil size & reactivity 
•
DO NOT place pressure on eye 
•
DO NOT place pad over eye 
•
DO NOT remove penetrating object/foreign bodies 
•
DO NOT try to clean the eye 
 
Key initial management 
•
Cover with protective shield (e.g. plastic shield/cup 
•
Keep NPO 
•
IV Kefazolin & oral Ciprofloxacin 
•
ATT

CHEMICAL EYE INJURY 
 
Chemicals harmful to the eye: 
•
Alkalis (Lime, mortar, plaster, drain cleaner, oven cleaner, ammonia) 
•
Acids (Toilet cleaners, battery fluid, pool acid) 
•
Neutral (Solvents, detergents, aerosols, mace, pepper spray) 
History: 
•
Chemical involved 
•
Time of exposure 
•
First aid administered 
•
Symptoms – vision loss, pain, redness 
Examination (Should not delay management) 
•
Measure eye pH using Litmus paper 
•
Visual acuity 
•
Fundoscopy 
•
Intraocular pressure (tonometry) 
Emergency management 
•
Copious irrigation minimum 30 minutes, 3 L Normal Saline 
•
Topical anaesthetic drops should not delay irrigation 
•
Continue irrigation until pH of tears = 7.5 
•
Urgent Ophthalmology referral
